verdict.rationale: Unity's core Editor and Player install and run on the user's own machines. The docs cover headless/batchmode operation and a standalone CLI aimed at your own CI build agents (unity-docs-8, unity-docs-26, unity-probe-rt-3, unity-probe-rt-4), so the core tooling can run on user-controlled infrastructure. However, nothing frames this as self-hosting. Community reports describe a license phone-home dependency and per-seat licensing that blocked setting up a build server (unity-comm-3, unity-comm-6). AI features and Build Automation are vendor-hosted, metered services (unity-docs-14, unity-docs-28). Missing for 10: documented self-hosted or offline deployment of the core product independent of Unity's licensing servers, self-hostable equivalents of the cloud services, and an open or redistributable source distribution.
